summary: Design baseline frozen: the approved evaluator design and its review packet are committed with a dated changelog so future design edits are reviewable diffs.

Audited the approved first implementation slice: most of it already exists in the repo; remaining gaps are schema contract coverage, site profile cache metadata, generalized manifest validation, and a reproducible resume check.

Design baseline is committed and the gap audit is done; now implementing the remaining slice pieces (schema contracts, site profile cache, generalized validation, resume check) before the bounded Dress Up pilot run.

First implementation slice is complete and committed: schema contracts, platform self-checks, plugin architecture, Shopify adapter, checkpointed runner, site profile cache evidence, and new resume and parity validators all pass static validation.
Dress Up pilot succeeded: the bounded five-query inspection reached 100 percent evidence coverage and matched the earlier rendered-browser evidence on all ten search and autocomplete checks.

Resume validation passed: a deliberately interrupted Dress Up run resumed from its checkpoint, reused the completed search work and site profile without re-fetching, and finished the remaining plugins live.
Handoff written covering what was built, the pilot results, validation status, and next steps for the stream.

Delegated task complete: design baseline frozen, first implementation slice built and validated, Dress Up pilot passed with full parity to prior evidence, resume behavior proven, and the handoff is written; work is in four local commits awaiting push approval.

Starting the in-app dataset viewer for the inspection dashboard so you can browse evaluations, targets, query packs, site profiles, platform registries, inspection history, and generated run datasets without leaving the dashboard; also recorded your keep-it-local directive, so nothing gets pushed or deployed.

The dashboard now has a Datasets tab that browses evaluations, targets, query packs, site profiles, platform registries, inspection history, and generated run datasets as searchable, filterable tables with per-record detail, and inspection findings link straight to the underlying records.

All validation passed: the extended dashboard validator, the full generation suite, the legacy framework validator, and a live browser walkthrough of tab switching, deep links, search filtering, record detail, and finding-to-dataset links; recorded as validation run fifty-two, which restarts the gate clean-pass count at one because implementation changed.

Delegated dataset viewer task complete: reach it via the Datasets tab on the local dashboard or any View link from an inspection, the handoff note is written, rendered page capture and browse-graph extraction were left untouched as instructed, and everything stays local per the keep-it-local directive.

Ferosh resolved all three open clarification decisions with the recommended options: retain all raw evidence per inspection by default, keep timestamp-based inspection IDs, and gate broad inspections at Shopify discovery maturity for Shopify targets while rendered capture gates everything else; the decisions are recorded in state, the validation strategy, and the decisions document, leaving no open clarifications for this generation.

On the operator's instruction everything was committed and pushed to the private GitHub repo, the bounded Ridge blocked-domain pilot ran and correctly reported a partial low-confidence inspection with explicit limitations, the Dress Up pilot reran with full parity, and the second independent Validation Gate pass is clean, meeting the two-pass requirement.

Only the generation thirteen BDD inventory refresh remains before phase exit; after that the next delegated step is rendered page capture and browse graph extraction, which now formally gates non-Shopify targets per the operator's third decision.

Generation thirteen phase exit is declared: the refreshed BDD inventory grades twenty-six scenarios with twenty-three passing, none failing, and three deferred with revisit conditions, on top of the two clean gate passes; everything is committed and pushed, and next-generation routing is open with rendered page capture and application-generated executive reports as the leading candidates.

The full cycle now works inside the app: the operator adds an ecommerce site by URL on the dashboard, the inspection runs automatically, and one click generates an executive report built only from the retained inspection evidence; this was proven live end to end on a real boutique store added through the UI.

Generation fourteen is chartered around the full-cycle application; the first gate pass is clean and the queued follow-ups are catalog-derived query packs, PDF rendering for the executive report, maturity enforcement at onboarding, rendered page capture, and fix-assist workflows.
